label: Explanans level explains a contrast: its actual choice cell excludes the rival outcome
term: explains a contrast (determination on choice cells)
definition: ExplainsContrast a h out y is Cstit a h (out ≠ y): every history through the moment that agrees with the actual history h on the explanans of level a (lies in a's actual choice cell) has an outcome other than y. SelectsActual a h out is Cstit a h (out = out h). CellRange a h out is the set of outcomes realized in a's actual cell; RealizedRange out is the set of outcomes realized by any history of the scope. A level of explanation of one source (its invariant nature, or its actual exercise) is represented as a STIT agent whose cells are the classes of histories agreeing on that level's explanans.
note: Stipulated in order to compare accounts under one contrastive standard (#2145, Lane 2). It is the determination test: a reason false at every rival history, in the family of SELECTING_AN_OUTCOME_2 (ContrastRelevant, DEF b64af87d), here typed on choice cells rather than on fact arenas. It does not say that determination is the only kind of explanation; pro tanto favouring (SELECTING_AN_OUTCOME_1) and teleological explanation are other explananda. See docs/notes/optimal-creation-choice.md §59. SelectsActual and ExplainsContrast are not senses of DISAMB 59b60fe6 (Selecting an outcome) and are not bridged to ContrastRelevant; they are the cell-level analogue of its second sense. A level whose cells are the outcome partition meets them trivially (SelectionRangeLaws law 8).
